A1.justification: Both PDFs describe URLOST and retain corresponding methods, datasets and experiments. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original representation-learning results on CIFAR-10 variants, V1 neural responses and TCGA gene expression, together with component ablations and learned-weight visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds comparison methods, masking and hyperparameter studies, noise experiments and computational benchmarks.

M1.justification: The clustering, self-organizing layer and masked-autoencoder pipeline remains intact. However, the stated density rule changes from a full affinity sum and p(i)=q(i)^(-alpha)n(i)^beta in v1 to a top-K sum and p(i)=q(i)^alpha n(i)^(-beta) in v2 (Eq. 4). This revises the written clustering prescription; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments used the revised expression.

E1.justification: The original, permuted, foveated and locally permuted CIFAR-10 settings, V1 recordings and TCGA classification are retained. v2 adds Gaussian-noise-corrupted CIFAR-10 as a distinct input condition for topology-recovery analysis (Appendix A.11), without adding another data domain or classification task.

E2.justification: v2 adds SimCLR with the Vision GNN backbone, ViG, to all three image comparisons in Table 1. It also introduces random-grouped masking comparisons in Tables 2–3, while retaining individual-dimension MAE results in Table 3. The existing ResNet-18 SimCLR, raw-signal and beta-VAE comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2's main V1/TCGA MAE comparison specifies random dimension groups, while Table 3 retains the earlier individual-dimension results. New evaluation procedures include TCGA clustering-parameter sweeps, distance-averaged mutual information under Gaussian noise, and preprocessing and module-runtime benchmarks (Appendices A.7, A.9 and A.11). Linear probing and TCGA five-fold validation remain; newly disclosed training budgets do not establish changes to existing runs.

E4.justification: The projection-sharing, density-adjustment and weight-evolution analyses are retained. v2 adds clustered versus random versus individual masking (Section 4.1), TCGA clustering-hyperparameter sensitivity, noise robustness of topology recovery, and computational-cost and parameter-overhead analyses. These substantially expand testing of mechanisms, sensitivity and practical limitations.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates and TCGA five-fold averages without seed counts or confidence intervals. v2 Table 2 first reports 15 randomly selected seeds and 95% confidence intervals for the natural-data comparisons; Table 7 averages timing over 500 trials. The earlier version does not establish a run count from which an increase can be inferred.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 scores remain, while ViG adds 53.8%, 40.0% and 42.8% across its three image settings. Table 2 updates results, including URLOST V1 decoding from 78.2% to 78.75% and raw TCGA accuracy from 91.1% to 91.7%. MAE's masking setting changes, preventing a same-setting gain interpretation. New masking, sensitivity, noise and runtime results substantially expand the evidence.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit discrete trace objective in Section 2.2, measure and absolute-continuity assumptions with a Radon–Nikodym derivation in Appendix A.1, and formal graph-topology and group-based stationarity definitions in A.8. This substantially expands the mathematical treatment beyond v1's shorter continuum formulation. The inverse-permutation proof is retained in A.5 rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: Both abstracts, introductions and concluding discussions present the same central contribution: learning representations without prior knowledge of topology or stationarity using clustering, self-organization and masked autoencoding, demonstrated across synthetic vision, neural responses and gene expression. The additional evidence does not redefine this core claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting alignment to attention inner products and possible positional transformations, and interprets the new sensitivity and noise findings. Section 6 and Appendices A.9–A.10 explicitly qualify applicability through quadratic preprocessing costs, difficulties beyond approximately 10,000 dimensions and limited dataset scale. These provide substantive boundaries absent from v1's broader future-work discussion.

D1.justification: v1 provides sampling and clustering procedures but little training specification. v2 Appendix A.6 adds optimizers, learning rates, schedules, epochs, network depths, hidden dimensions and dataset-specific clustering parameters. It also documents a correlation fallback, identifies timing hardware and adds a code-repository link. These improve documented reproducibility without establishing that every newly specified setting changed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning relative to Vision GNN, PatchGT, FlexiViT, Perceiver, Perceiver IO and self-guided masked autoencoders, alongside GNN scaling and random-field literature. It elaborates the already-cited Kohonen self-organizing map and gives specific methodological distinctions in Section 5 and Appendix A.12, replacing v1's comparatively brief treatment.

P1.justification: The introduction, clustering exposition, alignment rationale, related work and discussion undergo substantial rewriting. The continuum motivation moves into Appendix A.1, the ablation narrative gains a masking-unit subsection, and the appendices are reorganized around implementation, definitions and practical limitations. Author information, acknowledgements and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds masking-unit Table 3, parameter and timing Tables 6–7, and sensitivity, runtime and noise Figures 7–9. Existing comparison tables expand and the document adopts the ICLR layout. Earlier visual evidence is retained: notably, v1's weight-evolution Figure 7 becomes v2 Figure 10 rather than representing a new analysis.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support and reproducibility through repeated-seed confidence intervals, direct masking controls, detailed training settings and measured computational limitations, addressing important gaps in v1. Reporting remains imperfect: random-grouped MAE scores differ between Tables 2 and 3 without reconciliation, Appendix A.6 describes individual-dimension masking, and the revised density equation conflicts with retained explanatory prose. These ambiguities limit reproducibility, but the stronger validation and explicit applicability limits provide a substantial net improvement.
